title: Gamecocks open season against Bulldogs with offensive records
seoTitle: Gamecocks Open Season Against Bulldogs With Records
subtitle: South Carolina starts the SEC season with historic wins and scoring records
excerpt: South Carolina begins the SEC season with two blowout victories, setting scoring records and offensive pace.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
South Carolina opens the college football season with two blowout victories, setting scoring records and offensive pace. The team, led by head coach Shane Beamer, continues a 19-game sellout streak at Williams-Brice Stadium, the eighth-longest active streak in the country.

Historic season-opening victories

  • Secured a 45-9 win over Towson and 57-0 against Kent State, totaling 102 points in the first two games, the highest total since 1980.
  • The 57-0 win against Kent State was the largest margin of victory in a season opener in program history, surpassing the 53-0 mark from 1938.
  • Beamer's team reached 8-0 on the season and has 33 wins in the first five seasons, the third-highest mark in program history.

Punt return and rushing records

  • Super Swain, an All-SEC punt returner, broke Dick Harris's 55-year-old record by scoring two return touchdowns in a single game, totaling five career punt return touchdowns.
  • South Carolina rushed for 416 yards in a game, the third-highest single-game rushing yards mark in program history.
  • The rushing offense of 341.5 yards per game ranks third in the SEC and third nationally.

Dominant defense and points allowed records

  • Allowed only one touchdown in the first two games of the season, ranking first in scoring defense in the SEC.
  • Allowed just 179 total yards in the 57-0 win against Kent State, demonstrating the team's defensive solidity.
  • Defensive coordinator Clayton White has the team ranked 8th in total defense, allowing 191.0 yards per game.

Stadium renovation and fan experience

  • Phase I of the $350 million renovation of Williams-Brice Stadium is complete, bringing improvements to the fan experience.
  • All tickets will be digital, with an interactive map available for fans.
  • The stadium continues to sell out all seats, maintaining the streak of 19 consecutive sellouts.

Preparation for the matchup against Mississippi State

  • The game against the Bulldogs is scheduled for 4:15 p.m. (ET) on Saturday, with South Carolina holding an 8-1 series advantage since 2000.
  • Commentary from analysts such as Matt Schumacker and Aaron Murray will accompany the game on the SEC Network.
  • The South Carolina team maintains the lead in points per game and rushing yards in the SEC.

With information from University of South Carolina Athletics.
